evals.name: heavy-ai-tells
evals.prompt: Can you do a prose review on this README? It feels a bit AI-generated and I want to clean it up before I publish. The file is at fixtures/heavy-ai-tells/README.md.
evals.expected_output: A violation report flagging at minimum: RULE-12 (long sentences), RULE-02 (passive voice), RULE-D (Furthermore overuse), RULE-B (em-dash filler), RULE-H (unsupported 'studies show' claim), RULE-F (DataFlow Pro / DFP / Data-Flow-Pro inconsistency), RULE-G (mixed heading case), RULE-I (contractions), RULE-04 (needless words), RULE-05 (cliches), RULE-A (over-bulleting). Skill should ask before editing.

evals.name: clean-prose
evals.prompt: audit this doc for AI tells please: fixtures/clean-prose/docs.md
evals.expected_output: Skill produces a clean-or-near-clean report. Should NOT hallucinate violations. Zero High-severity issues; at most a handful of Low-severity stylistic notes acceptable.

evals.name: multi-file-repo-scan
evals.expected_output: Skill globs *.md/*.mdx in cwd, scans README.md and docs/architecture.md, EXCLUDES node_modules/should-skip.md from the report, groups violations by file, flags issues in both included files (Furthermore-streak in README, em-dash filler and run-on sentences in architecture.md).

evals.name: out-of-scope-fiction
evals.prompt: review this story draft for AI tells: fixtures/out-of-scope/story-draft.md
evals.expected_output: Skill recognises the file as fiction (not technical prose) and pauses to confirm with the user before reviewing, per the 'What not to flag' guidance. Should not produce a violation report unprompted.
